recommendation: Keep the source change as the missing application of FHIR-19312. Future work group action should be a separate change request if a precise cache-TTL header grammar or CapabilityStatement discovery surface is desired.
issue_request: FHIR-19312 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification and requested documentation of an X-Consent HTTP header whose value is a URI to consent material authorizing a request, including client/server responsibilities, optional server support, retrieval/rejection behavior, short-lived caching/freshness concerns, async handling, and no discovery or CapabilityStatement mechanism.
initial_application: No prior application was found in current source or git history: searches for FHIR-19312 and X-Consent found no Jira-tagged source commit or existing source text, and R4/R5/current published Consent/Security pages sampled before the edit did not contain X-Consent wording.
additional_context: Zulip discussion immediately after the vote clarified that X-Consent is an optional request-side interoperability mechanism, not a mandate or response-direction header, and that servers remain responsible for policy decisions. Confluence minutes list the San Antonio WGM session for GF#19312, and no later final Jira issue was found that supersedes the applied decision.
reconciliation: Added an X-Consent Header section to source/consent/consent-notes.xml, which is in build scope through the active Consent resource. The new text defines the URI-valued request header, gives Consent/Binary/PDF examples, describes client and server responsibilities, optional processing and rejection, REST applicability with query/retrieve emphasis, async handling, short-lived or validated caching with revocation awareness, and the lack of a core discovery/CapabilityStatement mechanism.
source_changes: source/consent/consent-notes.xml: Added an X-Consent Header section documenting the optional URI-valued request header and its processing guidance.

related_jiras.note: Analogous Applied/Published X-Provenance header work shows FHIR already used X-* request headers, but it did not decide X-Consent.
